independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.78.1-Ps.78.8 re-derived independently. Ps 78 is an identity psalm on the offset map, and the bytes bear that out: MT 78:1 carries the genre labels מַשְׂכִּ֗יל לְאָ֫סָ֥ף before the body clause הַאֲזִ֣ינָה עַ֭מִּי תּוֹרָתִ֑י (both oshb:Ps.78.1, collate byte tier), so the title sits inside MT v1 and the web:Ps.78.0 = oshb:Ps.78.1 pairing is the owner-ruled title form, correctly used; being an identity psalm, no dual-cite is owed on the remaining cites, and citation_sweep.py returns GREEN. The 8|9 seam verifies on both witnesses: 78:8 closes on an unnamed collective while MT 78:9 opens on the named tribe בְּֽנֵי אֶפְרַ֗יִם (oshb:Ps.78.9, byte tier), the only subject change of that kind inside the span. Every WEB quote in the row verifies verbatim against verse_map_web under the checker's punctuation folding, including the ellipsis-split quote at web:Ps.78.6; check_web_quotes.py raises nothing on this row. The rejected_alternative (a break after web:Ps.78.4) is the right rival and is correctly refused. Confidence high is calibrated to the seam. What does not survive re-derivation is the row's one grammatical signal: the claim of purpose-clause particles at the openings of BOTH web:Ps.78.6 and web:Ps.78.7 is contradicted by the pointed bytes, and the error tracks the WEB rendering rather than the Hebrew. The span and the seam stand; the stated evidence for internal cohesion does not.

challenges.claim: The substrate signal asserts 'purpose-clause particles' opening both web:Ps.78.6 and web:Ps.78.7, but the pointed bytes carry a purpose particle at the opening of 78:6 only — 78:7 opens on a waw-prefixed prefix-conjugation verb — and the psalm contains exactly 1 verse with that particle.
challenges.evidence: MT 78:6 opens on לְמַ֤עַן (oshb:Ps.78.6, byte tier). MT 78:7 opens on וְיָשִׂ֥ימוּ (oshb:Ps.78.7, byte tier) — waw-conjunctive plus verb, not a particle. sweep.py --skel on the particle's skeleton, spliced from oshb:Ps.78.6: 1 verse in Ps 78 carries it (Ps.78.6); unit = verses. Both verses are rendered alike in English — “that the generation to come might know” (web:Ps.78.6) and “that they might set their hope in God” (web:Ps.78.7) — which is the likely source of the plural: an English-rendering-driven form claim, and the staged extract carries no morphology layer to have caught it. The underlying continuity (78:7 continuing the 78:6 purpose chain) is sound and can be argued from these same bytes; the plural-particle description cannot.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.78.9-Ps.78.11 re-derived and holds. The opening quote בְּֽנֵי אֶפְרַ֗יִם collates byte at oshb:Ps.78.9, and the closing bracket אֶ֝פְרַ֗יִם collates byte at oshb:Ps.78.67 — note these are NOT byte-identical to each other (the 78:67 token carries an extra accent), and the row does not claim they are: it quotes each at its own ref with its own tier, which is the correct form. The count claim re-derives exactly: sweep.py --skel with the tribe name spliced from oshb:Ps.78.9 returns 5 verses book-wide, MT-keyed and dual-cited where the psalm is not identity (oshb:Ps.60.9 = web:Ps.60.7, oshb:Ps.78.9, oshb:Ps.78.67, oshb:Ps.80.3 = web:Ps.80.2, oshb:Ps.108.9 = web:Ps.108.8), and exactly 2 inside this psalm (oshb:Ps.78.9, oshb:Ps.78.67) — the row scopes its figure to 'this psalm' and names the unit, so the count object is clean. All three WEB quotes verify verbatim; check_refs_mirror.py is GREEN, so the out-of-span verses argued in prose (web:Ps.78.65, web:Ps.78.67, web:Ps.78.72) are all carried in boundary_evidence_refs. Ps 78 carries no selah, no ketiv/qere, no inverted nun and no suspended letter in pmarks_Ps.json, so there is no disclosure owed anywhere in this cluster and none is falsely claimed; check_marks.py is GREEN. Confidence medium is well calibrated — the 11|12 seam is a register shift rather than a hard formal marker, and the row says so. Observation, not a defect: 'bracketing the composition' is rhetorically generous for verses 9 and 67 of a 72-verse psalm; the recurrence is real but the two poles are interior. Observation: the cross_part_phrasing_variation flag is logged orchestrator bookkeeping and I do not treat it as a defect.

Span Ps.78.12-Ps.78.16 re-derived and the span itself is right. The Zoan count is the strongest evidence in the cluster and it re-derives exactly: sweep.py --skel with the place name spliced from oshb:Ps.78.12 returns 2 verses book-wide (Ps.78.12, Ps.78.43), both inside this psalm, and the row names its unit. The opening quote בְּאֶ֖רֶץ מִצְרַ֣יִם שְׂדֵה צֹֽעַן collates byte at oshb:Ps.78.12, and the 78:43 form collates byte at its own ref. The 16|17 turn is real and I verified it independently. The row is also careful in the right places — it labels the 12/43 pair a candidate inclusio and explicitly demotes it to corroborating texture rather than a driver, which is the correct handling. Two things fall short of the campaign's evidence standard. First, the row carries two negative universals over the span without the digit-bearing sweep the gate requires; check_universals.py flags one of them. I re-derived both and they are TRUE, which is why this is low and not higher — the defect is unswept form, not a false claim. Second, an observation rather than a challenge: the adverb at oshb:Ps.78.17 is described as 'opening the very next verse' when it is the second token of that verse, the verse opening on a different word — the same positional looseness that recurs across this writer part and that I do challenge where it carries more weight.

challenges.claim: Two negative universals about web:Ps.78.12-web:Ps.78.16 — 'with no note of complaint or unbelief' and 'no adversative particle or negated verb interrupts' — ship without an adjacent digit-bearing sweep, which the campaign gate requires; check_universals.py flags the first.
challenges.evidence: check_universals.py over the row file returns flag_count 1, path [2].rationale, claim 'with no note of complaint or unbelief'. Re-derived sweep, unit = tokens over the 5 verses MT 78:12-16: 0 tokens whose skeleton matches the negative particle לֹא (oshb:Ps.78.30, byte tier) and 0 matching its waw-prefixed form וְלֹ֤א (oshb:Ps.78.8, byte tier). The claim is therefore true, and the fix is a digit, not a retraction. For contrast inside the same psalm, MT 78:30 opens on לֹא (oshb:Ps.78.30, byte tier) and MT 78:8 opens on וְלֹ֤א (oshb:Ps.78.8, byte tier), both outside this span.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.78.17-Ps.78.22 re-derived; the span and both seams hold. The opening quote וַיּוֹסִ֣יפוּ collates byte at oshb:Ps.78.17 and the 78:18 quote collates byte at its ref; the span-scoped absence claim for the adverb across web:Ps.78.12-web:Ps.78.16 re-derives correctly (the adverb stands in exactly 3 verses of this psalm — Ps.78.17, Ps.78.30, Ps.78.32 — and none of them is in 12-16). The 22|23 seam is real: MT 78:23 opens a fresh divine initiative rather than continuing the causal clause of 78:22. The recurrence counts are also right: sweep.py --skel with the verb spliced from oshb:Ps.78.18 gives 3 verses in this psalm and 4 book-wide, exactly as the row states, with the unit named. Two defects sit on top of otherwise sound work, and both concern how that fourth occurrence and the tier are described. The first is a tier claim the collator does not support; the second asserts a campaign relation type that the campaign does not carry. Neither touches the span, and neither is machine-caught — citation_sweep.py, check_marks.py and check_refs_mirror.py are all GREEN on this row — which is precisely why they need a reviewer.

challenges.claim: The row attaches 'byte tier' to a form it says recurs 'in the identical inflected form' at web:Ps.78.41 and web:Ps.78.56, but the quoted token is byte-true only at oshb:Ps.78.18; at both claimed recurrences it collates one tier down, at accent_stripped.
challenges.evidence: collate.py on the row's own quoted token וַיְנַסּוּ: oshb:Ps.78.18 -> byte, oshb:Ps.78.41 -> accent_stripped, oshb:Ps.78.56 -> accent_stripped. The tokens actually standing at those verses are וַיְנַסּ֣וּ (oshb:Ps.78.41, byte tier) and וַיְנַסּ֣וּ (oshb:Ps.78.56, byte tier), each carrying an accent the quoted form lacks. Under the tier discipline an identity claim across the three verses is accent_stripped-grade, not byte-grade, and the staged extract has no morphology layer to license 'inflected form' as a separate warrant. The one verse where the quoted bytes do recur exactly is oshb:Ps.106.14 (collate byte) — the occurrence the row places outside the psalm.

challenges.claim: The row types the fourth sweep hit as 'a typed cross-psalm relation', a status the campaign reserves for its enumerated doublets and the 9-10 pair; Ps 78 / Ps 106 is not among them, so the row asserts a relation type that is not attested.
challenges.evidence: The campaign enumerates 4 typed relations: the doublets 14=53, 40:13-17=70 (WEB) and 57:7-11 plus 60:5-12 = 108 (WEB), together with the 9-10 pair. Ps 78 / Ps 106 is in 0 of those 4. The fourth sweep hit is MT 106:14 וַיִּתְאַוּ֣וּ תַ֭אֲוָה בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַיְנַסּוּ אֵ֝֗ל בִּֽישִׁימֽוֹן (oshb:Ps.106.14, byte tier) — the same verb inside a different clause, with no doublet relation attested between these psalms. citation_sweep.py returns GREEN on the row, so nothing machine-checks this wording. Re-describing the hit as what the sweep actually shows — a lexical recurrence in a second historical psalm — would carry the same texture, and the same 'never a merge' restraint, without asserting a registry status.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.78.23-Ps.78.31 re-derived. The 22|23 and 31|32 seams both hold, and all three Hebrew quotes collate byte at their cited refs (וַיְצַ֣ו שְׁחָקִ֣ים מִמָּ֑עַל at oshb:Ps.78.23, the 78:30 clause at oshb:Ps.78.30, the 78:31 clause at oshb:Ps.78.31). Confidence medium is honest: this is the cluster's longest span and it deliberately absorbs an internal turn at 29|30, so the row's cohesion warrant has to carry real weight. That warrant is the craving vocabulary — and it is the one place in the row where no Hebrew appears, even though the evidence exists, is byte-clean, and is invisible in the English the row does quote. That is the challenge. Two further observations that I do not raise to challenges. The row calls web:Ps.78.29 the movement's 'opening' when the span opens at web:Ps.78.23; 78:29 is the close of the provision, not its opening. And the row says the 78:31 anger vocabulary echoes web:Ps.78.21 'through the shared root rather than a repeated clause' — the bytes show more than a root echo: MT 78:21 and MT 78:31 share a predicate frame, the same noun with the same verb and a following bet-phrase, which strengthens rather than weakens the row's own cohesion argument.

challenges.claim: The row's stated reason for holding the span as one strophe — the craving vocabulary shared across web:Ps.78.29 and web:Ps.78.30 — is an original-language claim carried with no Hebrew at all, and it is not visible in the WEB wording the row quotes, so as written the load-bearing warrant is unevidenced.
challenges.evidence: The two WEB verses share no English token for it: “He gave them their own desire.” (web:Ps.78.29) against “They didn't turn from their cravings.” (web:Ps.78.30). The shared item is MT-only — וְ֝תַֽאֲוָתָ֗ם (oshb:Ps.78.29, byte tier) and מִתַּאֲוָתָ֑ם (oshb:Ps.78.30, byte tier). sweep.py --skel with the suffixed form spliced from oshb:Ps.78.30, unit = verses: 2 verses book-wide, both in this psalm (Ps.78.29, Ps.78.30). The evidence is strong and available at byte tier; the defect is distributional — the row carries 3 ref-bound Hebrew quotes, at oshb:Ps.78.23, oshb:Ps.78.30 and oshb:Ps.78.31, and 0 at oshb:Ps.78.29, so the one signal that decides the span is the one left unquoted. The standing rule is to quote the original language for every boundary-relevant original-language claim, and this is the row's.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.78.32-Ps.78.39 re-derived; the span is right and the 39|40 seam is right. The quoted clause בְּכָל זֹ֭את חָֽטְאוּ ע֑וֹד collates byte at oshb:Ps.78.32, all five WEB quotes verify verbatim including the ellipsis-split quote spanning web:Ps.78.38-web:Ps.78.39, and the 3-verse sweep figure for the adverb re-derives exactly (Ps.78.17, Ps.78.30, Ps.78.32; unit = verses, digit and members both given). check_refs_mirror.py is GREEN. Confidence high is defensible on the seams themselves. The problem is the device the row builds on that adverb and then generalizes in device_notes. Re-derived from the bytes, the adverb is verse-initial in none of its three verses, and the row's own quoted clause is said to open on the word that in fact ends it; worse, the generalization sweeps in web:Ps.78.30, where the adverb governs a food clause rather than a sin verb and where the campaign's own row set places it in the interior of the span Ps.78.23-Ps.78.31 rather than at any opening. The device is a real lexical thread and worth keeping as texture; the positional and functional claims made for it are not supported.

challenges.claim: The adverb-as-opening-marker device fails on the bytes in both directions: the adverb is verse-initial in none of its three verses (the row's own quoted clause ends on the word it is said to 'open on'), and the device_notes universal that it 'marks the opening of every sin-turn' is contradicted at web:Ps.78.30, where it governs a food clause and sits interior to the neighbouring strophe.
challenges.evidence: Token positions in the staged maqaf-free extract: MT 78:17 the adverb is token 2 of 7, the verse opening on וַיּוֹסִ֣יפוּ (oshb:Ps.78.17, byte tier); MT 78:30 token 4 of 6, opening on לֹא (oshb:Ps.78.30, byte tier); MT 78:32 token 4 of 7, opening on בְּכָל (oshb:Ps.78.32, byte tier). The signal's own quoted clause בְּכָל זֹ֭את חָֽטְאוּ ע֑וֹד (oshb:Ps.78.32, byte tier) terminates on the adverb. Function diverges at the middle member: “Their food was yet in their mouths,” (web:Ps.78.30) attaches it to the meal, against “they still went on to sin against him,” (web:Ps.78.17) and “For all this they still sinned,” (web:Ps.78.32) where it modifies the sin verb — and web:Ps.78.30 is interior to Ps.78.23-Ps.78.31, so it opens no turn. The 3-verse count itself is correct; only the positional and functional claims built on it are not.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.78.40-Ps.78.42 re-derived. Both Hebrew quotes collate byte at their cited refs, and the row deserves credit for the hardest call in the cluster: it discloses that its own end-seam is cut across a live grammatical continuity rather than concealing it, and confidence medium matches that. I verified the continuity independently and it is real — MT 78:42 closes on a relative clause and MT 78:43 opens on the same relative particle, so the seam genuinely cuts a chain. The in-psalm figure for the exclamative (1 verse) is correct and the verse-initial claim is correct here. The book-wide figure is not: it is a raw skeleton-substring count that the row presents as a count of the interrogative, and two thirds of its members are a different word. That is the challenge, together with a quote-convention breach in the same field that check_web_quotes.py flags. Observation, not raised to a challenge because the row does disclose the continuity and does carry web:Ps.78.43 in its refs: the device_notes claim that web:Ps.78.42-web:Ps.78.43 'share one Hebrew relative-clause chain' is an explicit original-language claim carried without any Hebrew — it is true on the bytes, and quoting the shared particle at both refs would settle it.

challenges.claim: The book-wide figure of 9 verses is offered as the count of the interrogative-exclamative, but it is the raw count of a three-letter skeleton string; only 3 of the 9 verses carry the interrogative, the other 6 being the noun 'wisdom' and one unrelated verb.
challenges.evidence: sweep.py --skel with the query spliced from oshb:Ps.78.40, unit = verses, results MT-keyed: 9 verses book-wide. The pointed token standing at each hit, each byte tier at its own ref, dual-cited where the psalm is not identity: כַּמָּ֪ה (oshb:Ps.35.17, byte tier), חָכְמָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.37.30, byte tier), חָכְמָ֥ה (oshb:Ps.51.8 = web:Ps.51.6, byte tier), כָּמַ֣הּ (oshb:Ps.63.2 = web:Ps.63.1, byte tier), כַּ֭מָּה (oshb:Ps.78.40, byte tier), חָכְמָֽה (oshb:Ps.90.12, byte tier), בְּחָכְמָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.104.24, byte tier), חָכְמָ֨ה (oshb:Ps.111.10, byte tier), כַּמָּ֥ה (oshb:Ps.119.84, byte tier). Five of the nine are the noun 'wisdom' (oshb:Ps.37.30, oshb:Ps.51.8 = web:Ps.51.6, oshb:Ps.90.12, oshb:Ps.104.24, oshb:Ps.111.10) and one is a different verb (oshb:Ps.63.2 = web:Ps.63.1); the swept skeleton is a substring of that noun, which is exactly the toolkit's short-token homography hazard. The interrogative stands in 3 verses book-wide — oshb:Ps.35.17, oshb:Ps.78.40, oshb:Ps.119.84 — not 9. The in-psalm figure of 1 verse is correct and unaffected.

challenges.claim: The English gloss of the Hebrew interrogative is set in curly double quotes in a field carrying no web: ref, breaching the convention that reserves curly doubles for WEB text; check_web_quotes.py flags it.
challenges.evidence: check_web_quotes.py over the row file returns flag_count 1 — path [6].observed_substrate_signals[0], quote 'how often/how much', issue 'curly quote with NO web: ref in its field'. The convention is curly doubles for WEB text only, straight quotes for glosses and for row or tool wording; the fix is straight quotes on the gloss. WEB does read “How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness” (web:Ps.78.40), but the flagged span is the compound gloss, not that text, so the field cannot be cured by adding a ref.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.78.43-Ps.78.51 re-derived and the span is sound. The opening quote בִּשְׂדֵה צֹֽעַן collates byte at oshb:Ps.78.43, the Zoan sweep re-derives exactly (2 verses book-wide, both in this psalm, unit named), and the 51|52 seam is real — MT 78:52 turns from Egypt's affliction to the leading out of Israel, which is a genuine subject change rather than another catalogue item. The inclusio with web:Ps.78.12 is correctly demoted to corroborating texture. Confidence high is calibrated to the span. The defect is in the rationale's itemization of the catalogue, which misassigns one verse against both witnesses — and the row's own rejected_alternative describes that same verse correctly, so the row contradicts itself on the point. The span is unaffected; the description of the evidence inside it is not.

challenges.claim: The rationale itemizes web:Ps.78.47 among the locust plagues, but both witnesses put hail and frost at that verse and the locust terms at web:Ps.78.46 alone — and the row's own rejected_alternative describes 78:47 correctly as a vegetation plague, so the two descriptions contradict each other.
challenges.evidence: MT 78:47 יַהֲרֹ֣ג בַּבָּרָ֣ד גַּפְנָ֑ם וְ֝שִׁקְמוֹתָ֗ם בַּֽחֲנָמַֽל (oshb:Ps.78.47, byte tier) carries the hail term and the frost term and no locust term; WEB agrees — “He destroyed their vines with hail, their sycamore fig trees with frost.” (web:Ps.78.47). The locust terms sit one verse earlier: MT 78:46 וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לֶחָסִ֣יל יְבוּלָ֑ם וִֽ֝יגִיעָ֗ם לָאַרְבֶּֽה (oshb:Ps.78.46, byte tier), WEB “He also gave their increase to the caterpillar, and their labor to the locust.” (web:Ps.78.46). Sweep over MT 78:44-51 with queries spliced from oshb:Ps.78.46 and oshb:Ps.78.47, unit = verses: the locust pair occurs in 1 verse (Ps.78.46), the hail term in 2 (Ps.78.47, Ps.78.48). The row's rejected_alternative meanwhile groups 78:47 with vegetation against livestock at 78:48, which the bytes support; the rationale's grouping is the one that fails.
